_meta.principle: Every value verified against a primary source this session, or it is NOT a row — it goes in _pending. No unverified numbers ever enter the database.
_meta.loader_note: CC: load `benchmarks` into CostBenchmark (replacing placeholder rows), `parameters` into config or a parameters table, keep `_pending` visible in docs as the extraction backlog.

benchmarks.metric: Value of one QALY (quality-adjusted life year — one year of full health)
benchmarks.source: HM Treasury Green Book (2022 clarification, carried in DHSC supplementary health appraisal guidance)
benchmarks.method: Willingness-to-pay value for cross-government appraisal. NOTE: distinct from the NICE cost-effectiveness threshold (~£20–30k/QALY), which is a different instrument for a different decision.
benchmarks.notes: Price year stated as 20/21 in GB2022.

benchmarks.metric: Value of one WELLBY (a 1-point change in life satisfaction, 0–10 scale, for one person for one year)
benchmarks.source: HM Treasury, Wellbeing Guidance for Appraisal: Supplementary Green Book Guidance (Jul 2021)
benchmarks.method: Central £13,000; low £10,000, high £16,000. Losses and gains valued equally.
benchmarks.notes: central=13000 (store in method/notes since schema carries low/high).

benchmarks.source: HM Treasury / DfT (Carthy et al. willingness-to-pay lineage); live value published in DfT TAG Data Book table A4.1.1 'average value of accident prevention per casualty'
benchmarks.method: Stated-preference (willingness-to-pay), uprated annually by GDP per head.
benchmarks.notes: CONTESTED: published academic critiques of the 1999 evidence base (Thomas & Vaughan 2015) — surface this to users. Phase 2b: pin the current TAG A4.1.1 figure and update priceYear.

benchmarks.metric: Unit cost of one homicide (total economic and social cost)
benchmarks.source: Home Office, The economic and social costs of crime (2nd ed., Research Report 99, 2018)
benchmarks.method: Costs in anticipation + as consequence + in response; highest unit cost of any offence.
benchmarks.notes: Full per-offence table (rape, violence with injury, burglary, robbery, vehicle theft…) is Phase 2b extraction from horr99 Table 1 + the newer 'Economic and social costs of crime 2019 to 2020' publication.

benchmarks.metric: Total cost of crime, England & Wales (context figure: individuals + businesses)
benchmarks.method: Context/scale anchor, not a unit cost — useful for sanity-checking impact claims.
benchmarks.notes: Violent crime ≈ three-quarters of individual-crime costs from one-third of offences.
